title: The Lovers of the Banu Tayy

keywords: the lovers of the banu tayy
full_text:
In the rugged mountains of the Shammar desert dwelt the noble nomadic tribe of Tayy, famed for their chivalry and proud traditions. A valiant young warrior named Wasim loved his cousin Rayhana, a maiden whose beauty was matched only by her wisdom and skill with the bow.

A feud broke out between their respective clans over the grazing rights to a mountain spring. Rayhana’s father, seeking to sever the lovers, moved his tents forty leagues to the south, declaring that no warrior of Wasim’s branch should ever approach his campfire.

Wasim did not succumb to despair. Rather than seeking violent confrontation, he rode alone to the neutral assembly of the tribal elders during the sacred truce month. Standing before the council of the Banu Tayy, Wasim challenged the rival clan to a contest of chivalry:

'Let the feud be judged not by shedding the blood of kin, but by three trials of desert virtue: a trial of horsemanship, a trial of archery, and a trial of poetic generosity!'

Rayhana’s brothers accepted the challenge. In horsemanship, Wasim rode bareback across the rocky ridges with peerless balance; in archery, he split a willow wand at eighty paces; and in poetry, he recited an ode celebrating the ancient unity and valor of the entire tribe of Tayy, bringing tears to the eyes of the fiercest warriors.

Rayhana stepped forward before the elders, testifying with modest courage that her heart belonged to Wasim and that his valor had healed the tribal rift.

The chief of the council embraced both families, wiped away the boundary lines of the spring, and blessed their wedding amidst the singing of the entire tribe, proving that chivalric honor and patience can dissolve decades of tribal strife.
moral: Steadfast courage and chaste fidelity overcome the harshest desert trials, uniting noble hearts.
